messages.subject: secondary periods in gmultmix
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to use the gmultmix model for my data on fire salamanders,
but I don't know very well how to define the secondary periods.
The data consist on one samplig site, with 3 primary and 4 secondary
periods, so:

y<-matrix(c(
22,28,16,29, 13,18,16,21, 26,32,24,19), nrow=1, ncol=12, byrow=TRUE)

umf<-unmarkedFrameGMM(y=y, numPrimary=3,type="removal")

In the examples of the reference manual it is not very clear how to do
this work (or maybe I did not understant it very well).

Best regards

Pablo

Hi Pablo,

It appears that you formatted your data correctly, but you cannot estimate these parameters if you only have data from 1 site.

I guess the documentation should state that nSites and numPrimary must be greater than 1. Anyone want to help improve the docs????

Richard

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] secondary periods in gmultmix
parts:
Hi Pablo,

The likelihood of your data at the starting values is 0, so the log-likelihood is -Inf. You could try other starting values, but I think there is another problem here. Are you sure you used removal sampling? You would hope that the counts would decrease over time if you are removing indiviudals. If the counts don't decline, then that is evidence of extremely low detection probability, which would make these data very hard to model.

If on the other hand you did not use removal sampling, and these are just repeated counts, then you need a different model. In our recent Ecology paper we mention this "binomial" observation model, but it is not implemented in unmarked yet. However, you could use the Dail-Madsen model with dynamics='notrend'. This seems to work. See their paper in Biometrics for more details.



> pcountOpen(~1, ~1, ~1, ~1, umf, dynamics="notrend", starts=c(2, 0, 1), K=100)

Call:
pcountOpen(lambdaformula = ~1, gammaformula = ~1, omegaformula = ~1,
    pformula = ~1, data = umf, K = 100, dynamics = "notrend",
    starts = c(2, 0, 1))

Abundance:
 Estimate     SE    z P(>|z|)
     4.37 0.0941 46.5       0

Apparent Survival:
 Estimate   SE     z P(>|z|)
    0.175 1.53 0.114   0.909

Detection:
 Estimate    SE    z  P(>|z|)
    -1.13 0.117 -9.7 2.91e-22

AIC: 336.2782
